scope_covered: Affirmations de nouveaute et de positionnement de paper/paper_saga_to_muon.tex : section 2.4 (l. 267-274), tableau 1 (l. 137-183), l. 418-420, 442-447, 465-467, 606-609, section 4.2 (l. 652-663), les six occurrences de 'not found' (l. 270, 274, 420, 446, 656, 663), pour les huit contributions (Th. 1, Th. 2, Prop. 3(d), Prop. 4, Prop. 3(c)/table SAGA/(M2)/metrique figee, Prop. 5, (M7), (C1)-(C3)). Registres internes lus : muon/literature_check.md (verdicts, addendum du 18 nov.), bibliography/literature_review.md (sections 6, 8, 10), muon/findings.md, archive/muon/notes_spectral_theory.tex, archive/muon/report_spectral_muon_new.tex. Recherches propres du 20 nov. 2026 : 11 requetes WebSearch, 6 requetes API arXiv au niveau des resumes (jusqu'aux depots du 18 nov. 2026), 18 PDF arXiv lus aux passages cites, 10 pages de resume (dont 4 sans lecture du PDF). Script : paper/audit/checks/novelty_close_works.py. Bilan : 0 bloquant, 0 majeur, 8 mineurs, 3 nits ; aucune anteriorite contenant deja un resultat revendique.

findings.claim: at a constant length variance reduction does not remove the floor: with the SAGA estimator the iterates settle at a squared distance $3.8\,\eta^2$ [...] whereas the floor of minibatch Muon is linear in its learning rate ; With a table the cooldown converges; without one it freezes the iterate
findings.problem: La dichotomie (plancher quadratique en la longueur quand le bruit s'annule a l'optimum, plancher qui subsiste sous bruit additif, minimiseur atteint seulement si le taux tend vers zero) est publiee pour les pas de signe et normalises par Singh, Mishra et Raut (arXiv:2607.12360, 14 juillet 2026). Le papier ne les cite pas alors que la verification du depot les classe parmi les travaux les plus proches. La nouveaute reelle (table SAGA, pas polaire, taux lineaire) reste intacte.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2607.12360, resume (PDF) : 'sign-based and normalized methods [...] settle on a noise floor of order eta^2 and reach the minimizer only as the learning rate is driven to zero; any additive noise then reinstates a floor for every method [...] extend the floor to normalized SGD in dimension d > 1 by a scale-invariance argument' ; introduction : 'Cooldown is necessary'. Registres : muon/literature_check.md l. 1314 et 1345, muon/findings.md l. 174-175. Absent du .tex et du .bib (script novelty_close_works.py).
findings.proposed_fix: l. 658, after \cite{ma2026preconditioning}; insert: sign and normalized steps under noise that vanishes at the optimum settle at a floor of order $\mathrm{lr}^2$ and reach the minimizer only when the learning rate goes to zero \cite{singh2026same}; [bib: S. Singh, A. Mishra, S. Raut, Same Loss, Same Noise, Opposite Schedules: Noise Structure and Optimizer Normalization Jointly Determine Whether Learning-Rate Cooldown Helps, arXiv:2607.12360, 2026]

findings.claim: a SAGA table in the nuclear-scaled polar step, the reading \finding{M2} and a metric frozen from one polar decomposition were not found
findings.problem: Lue seule, la derniere clause affirme qu'aucune metrique figee issue d'une decomposition polaire n'a ete trouvee. CacheMuon reutilise sur plusieurs pas une transformee d'orthogonalisation deja calculee, appliquee lineairement. Ce qui n'a pas ete trouve, d'apres le registre du depot, c'est SAGA (ou SVRG) dans une telle metrique.
findings.evidence: Dev, Bohara, Takac, Horvath, arXiv:2606.16371 (15 juin 2026), introduction : 'we propose CacheMuon, a Muon variant that reuses a previously computed orthogonalization transform across optimization steps'. muon/literature_check.md l. 45 : 'CacheMuon reuses a polar transform but has no finite-sum estimator'.
findings.proposed_fix: and SAGA in a metric frozen from one polar decomposition were not found (Muon with a cached polar transform: \cite{dev2026cachemuon}).  [variant without a new reference: and SAGA in a metric frozen from one polar decomposition were not found.]

findings.claim: A permutation order was seen to help SAGA-type methods with Finito \cite{defazio2014finito}, and linear rates are proved for reshuffled and cyclic orders \cite{ying2017variance,park2020linear}
findings.problem: Ying, Yuan et Sayed observent que SAGA sous permutation converge plus vite que sous tirage uniforme et donnent le mecanisme que (M7) reprend ('refreshes every entry once per pass'). Le papier ne leur attribue que la preuve du taux lineaire et rattache l'observation a Finito seul. Le gain chiffre (rho_star, de e^-1 vers e^-2) n'est pas dans leur article.
findings.evidence: arXiv:1708.01383 : 'This is because random reshuffling updates every history variable during each run, while uniform sampling may leave some variables [...] untouched. As we are going to illustrate in later experiments, this difference helps explain why SAGA under random reshuffling tends to have faster convergence rate.'
findings.proposed_fix: A permutation order was seen to help Finito \cite{defazio2014finito} and SAGA, where it refreshes every table entry in each pass \cite{ying2017variance}; linear rates are proved for reshuffled and cyclic orders \cite{ying2017variance,park2020linear},

findings.problem: Exact mais muet sur K=1, d>=2 : pour une sortie scalaire, le gradient par echantillon tronque d'un modele lineaire generalise convexe est le gradient d'une perte Huberisee de pente B/||x|| ; la normalisation (limite B->0) donne |<theta,x>-y|/||x||, soit Lambda pour K=1. Le passage a la limite est ma lecture, pas un enonce de l'article.
findings.evidence: Song, Steinke, Thakkar, Thakurta, arXiv:2006.06783v2, section 5.1 'Characterizing Clipping in Convex GLMs', Lemme 5.1 : g_x affine de pente +-B/||x||_2 hors de [y1,y2] et 'd_theta l_g(theta;x) = { min{1, B/||u||_2} u : u in d_theta l_f(theta;x) }'.
findings.proposed_fix: for $K=1$ it is the zero-threshold limit of per-sample clipping, a Huberized loss \cite[Lemma~5.1]{song2020evading}; for $K,d\ge2$ (d) was not found.

findings.claim: any advantage of another norm is a property of the trajectory
findings.problem: Le complement positif du theoreme 1 est publie : Davis et Drusvyatskiy donnent une condition par couche et par pas comparant le rapport nucleaire/Frobenius au carre du gradient (le 'nuclear rank' utilise l. 500-501 sans attribution) au rang stable des activations. Cite dans les notes du depot, pas dans le papier.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2512.04299, resume (lu par l'outil de fetch, resume seul) : 'propose a simple layerwise condition that predicts when a spectral update yields a larger decrease in the loss', comparant 'the squared nuclear-to-Frobenius ratio of the gradient' a 'the stable rank of the incoming activations'. archive/muon/notes_spectral_theory.tex l. 290-291.
findings.proposed_fix: and any advantage of another norm is a property of the trajectory (a per-step criterion is in \cite{davis2025when}).

findings.claim: finite-sum estimators in fixed-length polar steps \cite{li2026implicit} [...] are published
findings.problem: Le message de tete 'variance reduction acts on the fixed point' a une forme publiee sur donnees separables : pour la descente la plus raide en lots (norme spectrale comprise), la reduction de variance supprime la dependance de la limite a la taille du lot. Le papier cite cet article trois fois sans dire ce resultat.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2602.11557v2, resume : 'we prove that variance reduction can recover the exact full-batch implicit bias for any batch size, albeit at a slower convergence rate' ; apres le Th. 4.7 : 'variance reduction removes the dependence of the implicit bias on algorithmic parameters such as the batch size and momentum'.
findings.proposed_fix: finite-sum estimators in fixed-length polar steps, where they restore the full-batch limit direction on separable data \cite[Theorem~4.7]{li2026implicit},

findings.claim: the version of Proposition~\ref{prop:schedule} with a SAGA table, and its parts (a) and (c), were not found
findings.problem: Pour (a) le papier nomme les travaux proches (section 4.2) ; pour (c) aucun, alors que la verification du 18 novembre classe (c) 'CLOSE' : la normalisation de l'etat par le pas, donnant une chaine de Markov homogene pour un algorithme invariant d'echelle, est la technique d'Auger et Hansen ; Singh et al. ont un lemme d'invariance d'echelle.
findings.evidence: muon/literature_check.md l. 1312-1317 et 1351. Auger-Hansen, arXiv:1310.7697 (SIAM J. Optim. 2016), resume (outil de fetch, resume seul) : 'On scaling-invariant functions, we show the existence of a homogeneous Markov chain' ; convergence lineaire globale 'expressed in terms of different stability conditions of the normalised homogeneous Markov chain'.
findings.proposed_fix: l. 660, after 'are close to Proposition~\ref{prop:schedule}(a)' insert: , and the normalization of (c) is that of scale-invariant randomized search \cite{auger2016linear}

findings.claim: in dimension one Muon need not converge under skewed noise \cite{do2026muon}
findings.problem: Le theoreme 1.2 de Do, Dereich et Jentzen porte sur des parametres matriciels (avec momentum et Newton-Schulz generalise) et borne l'erreur quadratique moyenne par C(1/M + gamma_n) : pendant publie de la Prop. 3(b) (ecart d'ordre 1/b) et borne que la Prop. 4 affine. Le papier ne retient d'eux que la dimension un.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2608.04607v1, Th. 1.2 : 'A = x_{i=1}^delta R^{d_i x d_i} [...] E||Theta_n - vartheta||^2 <= C(M^-1 + gamma_n)' (1.5) ; Th. 1.3 et Prop. 6.2 en dimension un seulement.
findings.proposed_fix: For Muon, \cite{do2026muon} bound the mean-square error by $C(1/b+\mathrm{lr}_t)$ for matrix parameters and, in dimension one, prove non-convergence under skewed bounded data and show that every limit is a zero of the mean field.

findings.claim: reshuffled SAGA-type methods \cite{ying2017variance,mokhtari2018surpassing} ; some beating $e^{-1}$ per pass for $\kappa<4.08$ \cite{mokhtari2018surpassing}
findings.problem: La methode de Mokhtari et al. (DIAG) est cyclique, pas a permutation aleatoire. Le seuil 4.08 n'est pas dans l'article : c'est un calcul du papier a partir du Corollaire 3 (rho^2 < e^-1).
findings.evidence: arXiv:1611.00347, resume : fonction 'chosen based on a cyclic scheme' ; Corollaire 3 : facteur rho=(kappa-1)/(kappa+1) par passe. bibliography/literature_review.md section 10.2 : 'a comparison not made in the papers'. Script : seuil 4.0830.
findings.proposed_fix: Table 1: reshuffled and cyclic SAGA-type methods \cite{ying2017variance,mokhtari2018surpassing}.  l. 608-609: and the cyclic rate of \cite[Corollary~3]{mokhtari2018surpassing} beats $e^{-1}$ per pass for $\kappa<4.08$.
